subject.title: Exec/tool failures show "(see attached image)" and suppress model response

question: For read-only exec-like or tool-error turns with no delivered user-facing reply, should OpenClaw surface a concise tool-error warning, the incomplete-turn fallback, or keep the current suppression unless verbose/cron/heartbeat mode opts in?
rationale: Current main intentionally suppresses some exec-like warnings and all lastToolError incomplete-turn fallbacks, and changing that contract can create noisy duplicate warnings or unsafe retry expectations without maintainer intent.

options.title: Show concise no-reply warnings
options.body: Surface a compact warning only when no user-facing reply was delivered, while keeping raw details limited to existing full/cron/heartbeat modes.

options.title: Prefer incomplete-turn fallback
options.body: Let payloadCount=0 lastToolError turns use the existing incomplete-turn fallback and reserve tool-error warnings for mutating or detailed modes.

options.title: Keep current suppression
options.body: Accept that some read-only exec/tool failures remain silent unless live repro proves the warning noise is worse than the missing reply.

recommendation.title: Show concise no-reply warnings
recommendation.body: Surface a compact warning only when no user-facing reply was delivered, while keeping raw details limited to existing full/cron/heartbeat modes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent terminal-classifier work is the broadest ownership signal for the remaining warning versus fallback contract.
